summary: A cabin lookout on Peters Mountain, WV, built in 1934 and burned in 1996; closed to entry since November 2024, with a federally funded rebuild planned.

facts.design: Cabin built atop slab-like sandstone boulders; 1956 state lookout with a live-in cab on U.S. Forest Service plans
facts.status_note: Standing, but the building has been closed to the public since November 2024 after a Forest Service inspection found the decking and support arches unstable.

access.note: The trail is open for hikers, but the public may not enter the building. Forest Service said the area may close once construction starts; work could begin as soon as September 30, 2026.

visit.trail_note: About a mile on foot from the nearest parking lot on Peters Mountain. The trail is open; the building is closed.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, George Washington and Jefferson National Forest

corrections.proposed: 1934 built (CCC volunteers' hut; register says WV Division of Forestry); 1956 larger lookout; 1997 rebuilt after 1996 fire
corrections.why: The register's Built field says 1997, but its own description says the lookout was built in 1934 and reconstructed in 1999. The Gazette-Mail places the 1997 rebuild after the 1996 fire.
The 2020 report says new boards and windows were installed. It does not describe a full restoration.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's Built field (1997) conflicts with its own description (built 1934). The Gazette-Mail's CCC-hut account also points to 1934. The story gives 1934 as the first build and 1997 as the rebuild.

Three dates appear. The lookout history site says a new cabin was completed in May 1996. The Gazette-Mail says it was rebuilt the following year (1997). The register says reconstructed in 1999. The story reports the disagreement without choosing one.

The register and lookout history site say fire detection ended in 1972. A 2020 report lists the tower among partial service or ready stand-by towers. The brief's record is silent on this; the story says the status is unclear.
The register and volunteers call it a tower, and the Gazette-Mail calls it a weathered cabin on a rock. The brief's kind is ground. The story uses the Gazette-Mail's description.
The register gives 3,681 ft (1,122 m). The Gazette-Mail gives 3,812 ft. The record keeps the register's figure; the story does not use an elevation.

notes_for_editor: Current closure and rebuild plan are well documented (Gazette-Mail 2024, RealWV 2026, volunteer site). The history is less certain: the register's Built field (1997) contradicts its own description (1934), and rebuild dates differ across three sources. The 2020 report names the FFLA in its own title, so the publisher credit is no longer inferred. Elevation differs between the register and Gazette-Mail. Register photos (credited to Brian Powell and Victoria Oliver) were not added; licences not checked. The RealWV figure of $130,000 in donations was not used. The trail length (about one mile) is from RealWV and the Gazette-Mail (a mile-long trek); the Gazette-Mail's wording was not used for access. Read budget ran to about six page reads plus one search.
